VIDEO.title: The Sin Religious People Don't Know They're Committing
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 2:17-3:8 · Episode 5 (#5 of 28 in the playlist)
hand: Circumcision of the heart, by the Spirit
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Romans 2:17-3:8. Paul addresses the one who bears the name 'Jew,' relies on the Law and boasts in God: a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness. Yet do you steal, commit adultery, rob temples? 'The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you' (2:17-24). Circumcision has value if you practice the Law; true circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit (2:25-29). Then an imagined objector asks what advantage the Jew has, and Paul answers (3:1-8).

The teacher reads 'Jew' here as Christians from a Jewish background in the Roman church (his shorthand: CJB), who looked down on Gentile-background believers (CGB) because they kept Torah. The answer to Paul's rhetorical questions is yes: they too are without excuse, setting up 'There is none righteous' (3:10) and 'there is no distinction' (3:22-23).

How could Paul know they were lawbreakers? A first-century Jew could look around: Israel was still in a kind of exile under pagan rule, which the prophets tied to covenant disobedience. Everyone needs deliverance, not only from Rome but from sin, death and the curse of Adam.

'Circumcision of the heart' is a Hebrew idiom for removing stubbornness and returning to God with the whole self: repentance (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4; 9:25-26). Yet Deuteronomy 30:6 says God will circumcise the heart. Human action and God's work are both-and, not either-or (Philippians 2:13; Galatians 2:20), with the clearest picture in Ezekiel 36:26-27.

In 3:1-8 the teacher color-codes the dialogue: the objector asks; Paul answers 'May it never be!' The Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God; their unbelief does not abolish 'the faithfulness of God' (3:3), the very idea he saw in 1:17. Paul draws on Psalm 116:11, Numbers 23:19 and Psalm 51:4. Other connections: Micah 3:11; Isaiah 42:6-7; 49:6; 60:1-3; Proverbs 6:23; Jeremiah 7:9-10; Hosea 4:1-2; Isaiah 52:5; Ezekiel 36:20-22.

The lesson: God is not impressed with external religious status. He wants a consistent life of faithfulness that flows from a heart shaped by His Spirit (compare Matthew 12:7; Hosea 6:6). Your religious identity means nothing if your life contradicts it. The teacher applies it to leaders who 'believe their own press,' and urges honest, proactive self-examination and accountability.
QUOTES: God is not impressed with external religious status. He wants to see a consistent life of faithfulness that flows out of a heart shaped by his spirit.
In God's eyes, your religious identity means nothing if your life contradicts it.
The biblical understanding of man's action and God's sovereign will is a both and. It's not an either or.
I never thought this would happen to me.

LSB_QUOTES.text: But he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that which is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; and his praise is not from men, but from God.
What then? If some did not believe, does their unbelief abolish the faithfulness of God?
“Moreover Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.

left.text: But if you bear the name “Jew” and rely upon the Law and boast in God, and know His will and approve the things that are essential, being instructed out of the Law,

right.text: Her heads pronounce judgment for a bribe, / And her priests instruct for a price, / And her prophets divine for money. / Yet they lean on Yahweh saying, / “Is not Yahweh in our midst? / Evil will not come upon us.”

lines.text: Paul finally names the 'Jew' in 2:17, though the teacher thinks he had this person in view since 2:1. Writing to a church, not a synagogue, he means Christians from a Jewish background who felt superior because they kept Torah.
Micah condemned corrupt leaders who still 'lean on Yahweh.' Relying on covenant status while failing to keep the covenant is an old sin.

NAME.title: A light to those in darkness

left.text: and are confident that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those who are in darkness, a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of the immature, having in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth,

right.text: “I am Yahweh, I have called You in righteousness; / I will also take hold of You by the hand and guard You, / And I will give You as a covenant to the people, / As a light to the nations, / To open blind eyes, / To bring out prisoners from the dungeon / And those who inhabit darkness from the prison.

lines.text: The images come from Isaiah 42, 49:6 and 60:1-3. Proverbs 6:23 names the source of the light: 'the commandment is a lamp and the law is light.' The Law is a guide to the blind and a light in darkness, and Paul uses that to correct those who carry it.

NAME.title: Do you steal? Do you rob temples?

left.text: you, therefore, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach that one shall not steal, do you steal? You who say that one should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

right.text: Will you steal, murder, and commit adultery and swear while lying, and burn incense to Baal and walk after other gods that you have not known, then come and stand before Me in this house, which is called by My name, and say, ‘We are delivered!’—that you may do all these abominations?

lines.text: The answer to Paul's questions is yes. Hosea 4:2 lists the same sins: 'swearing of oaths, deception, murder, stealing, and adultery.' Robbing temples is a form of idolatry.

'The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you' (Romans 2:24) draws on Isaiah 52:5, 'My name is continually blasphemed all day long,' and Ezekiel 36:20-22, where Israel profaned God's holy name among the nations.

HEART.title: A Jew inwardly
HEART.stamp: By the Spirit, not the letter

src.text: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh. But he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that which is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; and his praise is not from men, but from God.

lines.text: To level the field, Paul says an uncircumcised person who keeps the Law's requirements will be 'counted as circumcision' (2:26). Circumcision has value only if it takes root in the heart.
Study note (added): circumcision was given to Abraham as 'the sign of the covenant' (Genesis 17:11). Paul does not despise the sign; he insists on what it signified.

left.text: So circumcise your heart, and stiffen your neck no longer.

right.text: Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh / And remove the foreskins of your heart, / Men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, / Lest My wrath go forth like fire / And burn with none to quench it / Because of the evil of your deeds.”

lines.text: Circumcision of the heart means removing stubbornness and returning to God with the whole self: repentance. Jeremiah 9:25-26 warns of those 'circumcised and yet uncircumcised,' since 'all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart.'

left.text: “Moreover Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.

right.text: Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will be careful to do My judgments.

lines.text: Deuteronomy 10 and Jeremiah 4 put the action on the person; Deuteronomy 30 puts it on God. Are you doing it, or is God? The teacher: man's action and God's sovereign will are both-and, not either-or. 'It is God who is at work in you, both to will and to work for His good pleasure' (Philippians 2:13); 'it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me' (Galatians 2:20).
Ask a first-century Jew, 'Did you choose God or did God choose you?' and he would say, 'Yes.' Ezekiel 36 is the clearest link to heart circumcision by the Spirit.

src.text: Then what advantage has the Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision? Great in every respect. First of all, that they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

lines.text: The objector: if you are right, Paul, what is Jewish identity worth? Paul: a great deal. Israel carried the privilege and responsibility of being entrusted with God's revelation, as the whole Old Testament shows.
Study note (added): Stephen calls the Law given at Sinai 'living oracles' (Acts 7:38), and Paul lists Israel's privileges in Romans 9:4-5.

left.text: What then? If some did not believe, does their unbelief abolish the faithfulness of God? May it never be! Rather, let God be true and every man a liar, as it is written, / “That You may be justified in Your words, / And overcome when You are judged.”

right.text: “God is not a man, that He should lie, / Nor a son of man, that He should repent; / Has He said, and will He not do it? / Or has He spoken, and will He not establish it?

lines.text: If some of Israel failed, is God's covenant faithfulness void? Never. The teacher notes 'the faithfulness of God' here as support for reading 1:17 as 'out of God's faithfulness into man's faith.'
'Let God be true and every man a liar' draws on Psalm 116:11 ('All men are liars') and Numbers 23:19, then quotes Psalm 51:4, David's confession: 'So that You are justified when You speak.'

left.text: But if our unrighteousness demonstrates the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is the God who inflicts wrath unrighteous? (I am speaking in human terms.)

right.text: May it never be! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?

lines.text: If my sin makes God look more righteous, how can He judge me? Paul flags this as a foolish human argument; if it held, God could judge no one, Gentiles included.
Then the worst version: 'Let us do evil that good may come' (3:8). Paul refuses to dignify it: 'Their condemnation is just.' He takes the question up again in Romans 6:1-2.

TERMS.def: Trusting covenant status and possession of Torah for security (Romans 2:17; compare Micah 3:11).
Profiting from pagan shrines while claiming to abhor idols (Romans 2:22); a form of idolatry.
A Hebrew idiom for removing stubbornness and turning to God with the whole self (Deuteronomy 10:16; Romans 2:29).
The written code as outward rule, contrasted with the Spirit's inner work (Romans 2:29; 2 Corinthians 3:6).
God's spoken revelation entrusted to Israel (Romans 3:2).
God's reliability to His covenant, not undone by human unbelief (Romans 3:3).
Paul's strong denial of a false conclusion, used twice here (Romans 3:4).

WORDS.gloss: To rob temples; commit sacrilege. Look up: BDAG, ἱεροσυλέω.
To slander, speak irreverently of God; blaspheme.
Oracle, divine saying. Look up: BDAG, λόγιον.
Here 'faithfulness' (of God); the same word as 'faith' in 1:17.
To circumcise. Look up: HALOT or BDB, מוּל.

BACKGROUND.p: Temples held treasure and votive gifts. Acts 19:37 shows that 'robbers of temples' was a recognized accusation. Deuteronomy 7:25-26 forbade Israel to take the silver or gold of idols.

The teacher says first-century Jews under Roman rule saw themselves in a kind of continuing exile, the result of covenant disobedience. Some scholars argue this widely; others think it overstated. Daniel 9 and Nehemiah 9:36-37 show the feeling of being 'slaves' in the land.

BACKGROUND.h: Paul quotes the Greek of Isaiah
BACKGROUND.p: Romans 2:24 follows the Septuagint of Isaiah 52:5, which adds 'because of you' and 'among the Gentiles.' Romans 3:4 likewise follows the Greek of Psalm 51:4 ('overcome when You are judged').

Questions and answers with an imagined partner (3:1-8) were a common teaching style. Paul raises objections his readers might have and answers them, sometimes briefly, saving full answers for later chapters.

DEBATES.p: The video: Christians from a Jewish background in the Roman church. Many commentators: the Jewish people generally, addressed through a diatribe partner, as part of Paul's case that all are under sin (3:9). The two readings agree that covenant status without obedience cannot save.
A hypothetical person used to make a point, or Gentile Christians who fulfill the Law by the Spirit (as the video read 2:14-15 last time).
Deuteronomy 10:16 and 30:6 set human and divine action side by side. The video holds both together rather than resolving the tension; Christian traditions explain the relation in different ways.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video gives the circumcision section as 'verses 24 to 28'; it is Romans 2:25-29.
The video's reading of Ezekiel 36 runs from verse 26 into verse 27 ('I will put My Spirit within you').
The video quotes Romans 3:4 as 'prevail when you are judged'; the LSB reads 'overcome when You are judged.' Paul follows the Greek of Psalm 51:4; the LSB of the psalm reads 'pure when You judge.'
'Still in exile' is a scholarly proposal the video presents as fact; it is debated.
CJB and CGB are the video's own shorthand, not terms from scholarship.

QUESTIONS: What religious status or reputation are you tempted to lean on?
Paul's questions (2:21-22) expect the answer yes. Which one presses on you?
What does circumcision of the heart look like in daily life?
How do you hold together 'circumcise your heart' and 'God will circumcise your heart'?
Who holds you accountable, and how could you make that more honest?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: God is not impressed with external religious status. He wants a consistent life of faithfulness that flows out of a heart shaped by His Spirit. Jesus told the Pharisees, quoting Hosea 6:6, that if they had known what 'I desire compassion' means, they would not have condemned the innocent (Matthew 12:7). The teacher turns it on himself and other leaders: pastors and teachers can start to believe their own press, until outward work for Jesus becomes a mask. Outward obedience never covers sin; the blood of Christ does. So he stays under accountability and practices regular self-examination, putting off the old self (Ephesians 4:22; Colossians 3:5). His mentor worked with leaders who had fallen, and the most common thing they said was, 'I never thought this would happen to me.'
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): this week, ask one trusted believer a direct question: 'Where do you see a gap between what I say and how I live?' Listen without defending yourself, and pray Psalm 51:10.

## The name of God blasphemed
1. Romans 2:17; Micah 3:11: Leaning on the Law

   Micah (Micah 3:11, LSB): "Her heads pronounce judgment for a bribe, / And her priests instruct for a price, / And her prophets divine for money. / Yet they lean on Yahweh saying, / “Is not Yahweh in our midst? / Evil will not come upon us.”"
   (video) Paul finally names the 'Jew' in 2:17, though the teacher thinks he had this person in view since 2:1. Writing to a church, not a synagogue, he means Christians from a Jewish background who felt superior because they kept Torah.
   (video) Micah condemned corrupt leaders who still 'lean on Yahweh.' Relying on covenant status while failing to keep the covenant is an old sin.
2. Romans 2:19; Isaiah 42:6-7: A light to those in darkness
   Paul (Romans 2:19-20, LSB): "and are confident that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those who are in darkness, a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of the immature, having in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth,"
   Isaiah (Isaiah 42:6-7, LSB): "“I am Yahweh, I have called You in righteousness; / I will also take hold of You by the hand and guard You, / And I will give You as a covenant to the people, / As a light to the nations, / To open blind eyes, / To bring out prisoners from the dungeon / And those who inhabit darkness from the prison."
   (video) The images come from Isaiah 42, 49:6 and 60:1-3. Proverbs 6:23 names the source of the light: 'the commandment is a lamp and the law is light.' The Law is a guide to the blind and a light in darkness, and Paul uses that to correct those who carry it. (Isaiah 49:6; Isaiah 60:1-3; Proverbs 6:23)
3. Romans 2:21-24; Jeremiah 7:9-10: Do you steal? Do you rob temples?
   Paul (Romans 2:21-22, LSB): "you, therefore, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach that one shall not steal, do you steal? You who say that one should not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?"
   Jeremiah (Jeremiah 7:9-10, LSB): "Will you steal, murder, and commit adultery and swear while lying, and burn incense to Baal and walk after other gods that you have not known, then come and stand before Me in this house, which is called by My name, and say, ‘We are delivered!’—that you may do all these abominations?"
   (video) The answer to Paul's questions is yes. Hosea 4:2 lists the same sins: 'swearing of oaths, deception, murder, stealing, and adultery.' Robbing temples is a form of idolatry. (Hosea 4:1-2)
   (video) 'The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you' (Romans 2:24) draws on Isaiah 52:5, 'My name is continually blasphemed all day long,' and Ezekiel 36:20-22, where Israel profaned God's holy name among the nations. (Isaiah 52:5; Ezekiel 36:20-22)

## Circumcision of the heart
1. Romans 2:25-29: A Jew inwardly
   By the Spirit, not the letter Romans 2:28-29: "For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh. But he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that which is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; and his praise is not from men, but from God." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+2:28-29
   (video) To level the field, Paul says an uncircumcised person who keeps the Law's requirements will be 'counted as circumcision' (2:26). Circumcision has value only if it takes root in the heart.
   [Background] Study note (added): circumcision was given to Abraham as 'the sign of the covenant' (Genesis 17:11). Paul does not despise the sign; he insists on what it signified. (Genesis 17:10-11)
2. Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4: Circumcise your heart
   Moses (Deuteronomy 10:16, LSB): "So circumcise your heart, and stiffen your neck no longer."
   Jeremiah (Jeremiah 4:4, LSB): "Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh / And remove the foreskins of your heart, / Men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, / Lest My wrath go forth like fire / And burn with none to quench it / Because of the evil of your deeds.”"
   (video) Circumcision of the heart means removing stubbornness and returning to God with the whole self: repentance. Jeremiah 9:25-26 warns of those 'circumcised and yet uncircumcised,' since 'all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart.' (Jeremiah 9:25-26)
3. Deuteronomy 30:6; Ezekiel 36:26-27: Who circumcises the heart?
   Moses (Deuteronomy 30:6, LSB): "“Moreover Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live."
   Ezekiel (Ezekiel 36:26-27, LSB): "Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will be careful to do My judgments."
   (video) Deuteronomy 10 and Jeremiah 4 put the action on the person; Deuteronomy 30 puts it on God. Are you doing it, or is God? The teacher: man's action and God's sovereign will are both-and, not either-or. 'It is God who is at work in you, both to will and to work for His good pleasure' (Philippians 2:13); 'it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me' (Galatians 2:20). (Philippians 2:13; Galatians 2:20)
   (video) Ask a first-century Jew, 'Did you choose God or did God choose you?' and he would say, 'Yes.' Ezekiel 36 is the clearest link to heart circumcision by the Spirit.

## The objector and the faithfulness of God
1. Romans 3:1-2: Great in every respect
   Entrusted Romans 3:1-2: "Then what advantage has the Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision? Great in every respect. First of all, that they were entrusted with the oracles of God." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+3:1-2
   (video) The objector: if you are right, Paul, what is Jewish identity worth? Paul: a great deal. Israel carried the privilege and responsibility of being entrusted with God's revelation, as the whole Old Testament shows.
   [Background] Study note (added): Stephen calls the Law given at Sinai 'living oracles' (Acts 7:38), and Paul lists Israel's privileges in Romans 9:4-5. (Acts 7:38; Romans 9:4-5)
2. Romans 3:3-4; Numbers 23:19: The faithfulness of God
   Paul (Romans 3:3-4, LSB): "What then? If some did not believe, does their unbelief abolish the faithfulness of God? May it never be! Rather, let God be true and every man a liar, as it is written, / “That You may be justified in Your words, / And overcome when You are judged.”"
   Balaam (Numbers 23:19, LSB): "“God is not a man, that He should lie, / Nor a son of man, that He should repent; / Has He said, and will He not do it? / Or has He spoken, and will He not establish it?"
   (video) If some of Israel failed, is God's covenant faithfulness void? Never. The teacher notes 'the faithfulness of God' here as support for reading 1:17 as 'out of God's faithfulness into man's faith.'
   (video) 'Let God be true and every man a liar' draws on Psalm 116:11 ('All men are liars') and Numbers 23:19, then quotes Psalm 51:4, David's confession: 'So that You are justified when You speak.' (Psalm 116:11; Psalm 51:4)
3. Romans 3:5-8: Then why not do evil?
   The objector (Romans 3:5, LSB): "But if our unrighteousness demonstrates the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is the God who inflicts wrath unrighteous? (I am speaking in human terms.)"
   Paul (Romans 3:6, LSB): "May it never be! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?"
   (video) If my sin makes God look more righteous, how can He judge me? Paul flags this as a foolish human argument; if it held, God could judge no one, Gentiles included.
   (video) Then the worst version: 'Let us do evil that good may come' (3:8). Paul refuses to dignify it: 'Their condemnation is just.' He takes the question up again in Romans 6:1-2. (Romans 6:1-2)

## Key people
- The one who bears the name 'Jew': Relies on the Law and boasts in God; the teacher's 'CJB,' a Jewish-background believer. [Background] Many commentators read 2:17 as addressing Jews generally, using a diatribe partner.
- The objector of 3:1-8: An imagined voice pushing back; the teacher color-codes his lines. [Background] Paul's 'May it never be!' (Romans 3:4; 3:6) is his usual reply to a false conclusion.
- Paul: A Hebrew of Hebrews (Philippians 3), a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees (Acts 23), a student of Gamaliel. [Background] His audience at this point should catch the scriptural references he drops.
- Moses: Deuteronomy 10:16 and 30:6: circumcise your heart; God will circumcise your heart. [Background] Deuteronomy 30 looks past failure and exile to restoration.
- Jeremiah: Condemns stealing, adultery and false worship; calls for circumcised hearts. [Background] His temple sermon (Jeremiah 7) warned against trusting the temple while breaking the covenant.
- David: Psalm 51:4, quoted in Romans 3:4. [Background] Psalm 51's heading ties it to Nathan's rebuke after David's sin with Bathsheba.

## Places [Background]
- Jerusalem (named in the video): The temple of Jeremiah 7: 'this house, which is called by My name.'
- Rome: A church of Jewish-background and Gentile-background believers.
- Corinth: Where Paul writes.
- Ephesus: The town clerk: Paul's companions are 'neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess' (Acts 19:37).

## Key terms
- Rely upon the Law: Trusting covenant status and possession of Torah for security (Romans 2:17; compare Micah 3:11).
- Rob temples: Profiting from pagan shrines while claiming to abhor idols (Romans 2:22); a form of idolatry.
- Circumcision of the heart: A Hebrew idiom for removing stubbornness and turning to God with the whole self (Deuteronomy 10:16; Romans 2:29).
- The letter: The written code as outward rule, contrasted with the Spirit's inner work (Romans 2:29; 2 Corinthians 3:6). [Background]
- Oracles of God: God's spoken revelation entrusted to Israel (Romans 3:2).
- Faithfulness of God: God's reliability to His covenant, not undone by human unbelief (Romans 3:3).
- May it never be!: Paul's strong denial of a false conclusion, used twice here (Romans 3:4). [Background]

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Temple robbery: Temples held treasure and votive gifts. Acts 19:37 shows that 'robbers of temples' was a recognized accusation. Deuteronomy 7:25-26 forbade Israel to take the silver or gold of idols.
- 'Still in exile': The teacher says first-century Jews under Roman rule saw themselves in a kind of continuing exile, the result of covenant disobedience. Some scholars argue this widely; others think it overstated. Daniel 9 and Nehemiah 9:36-37 show the feeling of being 'slaves' in the land.
- Paul quotes the Greek of Isaiah: Romans 2:24 follows the Septuagint of Isaiah 52:5, which adds 'because of you' and 'among the Gentiles.' Romans 3:4 likewise follows the Greek of Psalm 51:4 ('overcome when You are judged').
- Diatribe again: Questions and answers with an imagined partner (3:1-8) were a common teaching style. Paul raises objections his readers might have and answers them, sometimes briefly, saving full answers for later chapters.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Who is the 'Jew' of 2:17? The video: Christians from a Jewish background in the Roman church. Many commentators: the Jewish people generally, addressed through a diatribe partner, as part of Paul's case that all are under sin (3:9). The two readings agree that covenant status without obedience cannot save.
- Who is the uncircumcised Law-keeper (2:26-27)? A hypothetical person used to make a point, or Gentile Christians who fulfill the Law by the Spirit (as the video read 2:14-15 last time).
- Sovereignty and responsibility Deuteronomy 10:16 and 30:6 set human and divine action side by side. The video holds both together rather than resolving the tension; Christian traditions explain the relation in different ways.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video gives the circumcision section as 'verses 24 to 28'; it is Romans 2:25-29.
- The video's reading of Ezekiel 36 runs from verse 26 into verse 27 ('I will put My Spirit within you').
- The video quotes Romans 3:4 as 'prevail when you are judged'; the LSB reads 'overcome when You are judged.' Paul follows the Greek of Psalm 51:4; the LSB of the psalm reads 'pure when You judge.'
- 'Still in exile' is a scholarly proposal the video presents as fact; it is debated.
- CJB and CGB are the video's own shorthand, not terms from scholarship.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What religious status or reputation are you tempted to lean on?
2. Paul's questions (2:21-22) expect the answer yes. Which one presses on you?
3. What does circumcision of the heart look like in daily life?
4. How do you hold together 'circumcise your heart' and 'God will circumcise your heart'?
5. Who holds you accountable, and how could you make that more honest?

## Application
- (video) God is not impressed with external religious status. He wants a consistent life of faithfulness that flows out of a heart shaped by His Spirit. Jesus told the Pharisees, quoting Hosea 6:6, that if they had known what 'I desire compassion' means, they would not have condemned the innocent (Matthew 12:7). The teacher turns it on himself and other leaders: pastors and teachers can start to believe their own press, until outward work for Jesus becomes a mask. Outward obedience never covers sin; the blood of Christ does. So he stays under accountability and practices regular self-examination, putting off the old self (Ephesians 4:22; Colossians 3:5). His mentor worked with leaders who had fallen, and the most common thing they said was, 'I never thought this would happen to me.'
- Study note (added): this week, ask one trusted believer a direct question: 'Where do you see a gap between what I say and how I live?' Listen without defending yourself, and pray Psalm 51:10.
